To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inositol is necessary for the mitogen induced activation of ODC, and this effect is reversed by the addition of inositol or inositol phosphatides, but not by any other inositol derivative tested.
the activation of O DC in T cells requires inositol, and that inositol‐phospholipids can substitute inositol in this process.
inositol is required for the mitogenic activation of ODC, and that inositol and inositol phosphatides can reverse the Li+ inhibition of the Con A‐stimulated activation of ODC.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular mechanisms by which inositol‐l,3,4,5‐tetrakisphosphate and inositol phosphoceramides are involved in the activation of ornithine decarbosylase by mitogenic ligands in human T lymphoblasts.
the role of inositol‐phospholipids in the transduction of mitogenic signals in T lymphocytes.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms involved in transduction of mitogenic signals in human T lymphoblasts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

mitogenic ligands induce an activation of ODC which is not dependent on inositol phosphatase activity. but rather on the generation of inositols, and inositol phospho‐lipids, which are required for the activation of the enzyme.
inositol‐phospholipids are required for the rapid activation of ornithine decaboxylase (ODA) by mitogens.
the mitogen‐stimulated activation of ODC requires inositol phosphatides, but is not dependent upon the generation of IP3 alone, diacyl glycerol alone, or the other inositol‐containing phospholipids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inositol phosphatase system is a major component of a signalling mechanism which transduces the mitogenic signals to the nucleus.
inositol‐1.4,5‐tris‐phosphate is a necessary but not sufficient messenger for mitogenesis.
inositol and inositol phosphatides are required for the mitogen induced activation of ODC, but the molecular mechanisms by which this occurs are not yet clear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inositol‐phospholipid metabolites are required for the rapid activation of the mitogenic pathway in T lymphocytes and that the generation of these metabolites is not mediated by IP3.
inositol‐l, 4,5‐tris‐phosphate, diacylgycerol and other inositol metabolite do not appear to be directly involved in the mitogen‐activated activation of ornithine decaboxylase in human T lymphocyte.
the inositol phosphatidyl‐inositol pathway plays an important role in the transduction of mitogenic signals.
